capitals.name: Xieng Khouang (Muang Khun)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Xieng Khouang'; the page does not date moves; the French later set up Xieng Khouang town elsewhere.

correction.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Phuan row; its Lan Xang shapes from 1363 and its Ngo Dynasty row hold the plateau). Infobox 'Established: 13th century'; the Tai Phuan 'migrated to the area that is now Laos during the 13th century'. The page gives no area and no frontier; the province is the reading.

correction.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1707 Muang Phuan entered into tributary relations with the Kingdom of Luang Prabang'; tributary to Vientiane for 37 years from 1751; 'In 1779 the Kingdom of Vientiane was captured by the Siamese'. The principality is the same plateau.

correction.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: status list 'Vassal to Siam (1848-1893)'; 'Under the terms of the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893, Muang Phuan came under French colonial protection'; 'In 1899, the Phuan regions lost autonomy'. The page does not say how the 1832 Vietnamese annexation ended.

region.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.note: 13th century: the Tai Phuan settle the Xiang Khouang plateau. The page dates the principality only to 'the 13th century' (infobox 'Established: 13th century'; legend of Chet Chuong, son of Khun Borom); 1250 is a mid-century placeholder.

region.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.note: c. 1353: Fa Ngum takes Muang Phuan into Lan Xang. 'In the mid-14th century Muang Phuan was incorporated into the Lan Xang Kingdom under King Fa Ngum'; the page gives no year, 1353 is the lan-xang dossier's date for Fa Ngum's conquests (that dossier quotes its Fa Ngum page: 'In 1353, he conquered Vientiane, Xiang Khouang and then Luang Phrabang'; not a page opened here). The infobox also calls it an 'autonomous principality (14th century-1791)'.

region.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.note: 1707: Lan Xang divides and Muang Phuan stands apart as a tributary of Luang Prabang. 'In 1707 Muang Phuan entered into tributary relations with the Kingdom of Luang Prabang'; from 1751 'for the next 37 years Muang Phuan remained a tributary to Vientiane'. The Luang Prabang dossier carries the vassal tint.

region.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.note: 1832: Dai Viet annexes Muang Phuan as Tran Ninh. 'In 1832 the Dai Viet annexed Muang Phuan and named the region Tran Ninh.' The page also has Dai Viet claims in 1434 (tributary) and 1478 (attempted prefecture).

region.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.note: c. 1848: Muang Phuan is again a principality, a vassal of Siam. The page lists 'Vassal to Siam (1848-1893)' and is silent on the end of Vietnamese rule; 1848 is the status list's year, the land and the counterpart are my reading.

region.text: Xiang Khouang province: the Xiang Khouang plateau and the Plain of Jars, the Tai Phuan principality

ledger.note: 1899: the Phuan regions lose their autonomy. 'Under the terms of the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893, Muang Phuan came under French colonial protection'; 'In 1899, the Phuan regions lost autonomy and became part of the French Protectorate of Laos'. Kham Ngon (1880-1899) was the last ruler.

wars.name: Haw invasions of Xiang Khouang
wars.outcome: Haw bands invaded Xiang Khouang in 1874 and carried off population in 1875-1876; no change of border.
wars.note: The page's ruler list gives 'Haw pirates invade Xiang Khouang in 1874'.

certainty.note: The plateau and the Plain of Jars are named; no page gives a frontier, and the principality was under one overlord or another for most of its life.

sources.title: Muang Phuan
sources.note: Infobox ('Established: 13th century', 'autonomous principality 14th century-1791'), incorporation into Lan Xang, 1434, 1478, 1707, 1751-88, 1832, 1848-93, 1874, 1893, 1899. No area figure.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-f and se-01-i. One page opened (the article of the state, 3+ border changes; budget 2-5, thin). Not settled: (1) the page's own statements conflict: 'incorporated into Lan Xang under Fa Ngum' in the mid-14th century and 'autonomous principality (14th century-1791)'; the lan-xang dossier draws Xiang Khouang inside Lan Xang until 1707, so here the principality drops out 1353-1706 (a vassal tint in the lan-xang dossier would be the better picture); (2) the 1250 start and the 1353 loss are confidence 1; the lan-xang dossier also has an undated 'Muang Phuan' gain from Dai Viet in 1363; (3) the 1832 annexation as Tran Ninh and how it ended are not in nguyen-dynasty's ledger (no mirror gain); the page lists Siamese vassalage from 1848, and ayutthaya/rattanakosin-kingdom has no mirror vassal event either; (4) tributary relations with Dai Viet (1434), Luang Prabang (1707) and Vientiane (1751-88) are in other dossiers' vassal pairs; (5) kingdom-of-luang-phrabang carries counterpart 'muang-phuan' for its 1707 vassal_start; french-indochina should carry a vassal pair from 1893.
